items.meaning: What is left over; the number left after dividing.

items.heading: Division as equal sharing
lines: Example: Ravi has 12 toffees. He shares them equally among 4 friends. Each friend gets 3 toffees. 12 ÷ 4 = 3.

items.heading: Division as equal grouping
lines: Division also makes equal groups of items.
Example: 10 flowers are arranged in groups of 2. 10 ÷ 2 = 5. We get 5 equal groups.

items.heading: Division as repeated subtraction
lines: Division means repeatedly subtracting the same number until we reach zero.
Example: 24 ÷ 4 = 6, since 24 − 4 − 4 − 4 − 4 − 4 − 4 = 0. We subtract 4 six times.

items.heading: Properties
lines: Any number ÷ 1 = the same number. Example: 3 ÷ 1 = 3.
Any number ÷ the number itself = 1. Example: 3 ÷ 3 = 1.

sections.title: Practice: Divide and Find the Quotient and Remainder

items.question: Ayesha spends ₹96 on 8 pencils. How much money did she pay for each pencil?
items.answer: Cost of 1 pencil = ₹96 ÷ 8 = ₹12. So, Ayesha paid ₹12 for each pencil.

items.question: Reena has to put 63 empty bottles in 3 crates. How many bottles will she put in each crate?
items.answer: 63 ÷ 3 = 21. So, Reena will put 21 bottles in each crate.

items.question: A week has 7 days. How many weeks are there in 84 days?
items.answer: 84 ÷ 7 = 12. So, there are 12 weeks in 84 days.

items.question: A bus has 52 seats. Find the total number of rows in the bus if each row has 4 seats.
items.answer: 52 ÷ 4 = 13. So, the total number of rows in the bus is 13.

items.question: Aditya has 92 toy cars. He puts them equally in 6 boxes. How many toy cars will he put in each box? How many toy cars are left over?
items.answer: 92 ÷ 6 = 15, remainder 2. So, Aditya will put 15 toy cars in each box and 2 toy cars will be left over.

items.question: Reema sticks 5 pictures on a page. If she has 560 pictures, how many pages will she need?
A fruitseller buys 435 apples. He arranges them equally in 9 boxes. How many apples does he put in each box? How many apples are left over?
items.answer: 435 ÷ 9 = 48, remainder 3. So, he puts 48 apples in each box and 3 apples are left over.

items.question: An auditorium has to be filled with 228 chairs. How many chairs are needed in each row if there are 7 rows in total? How many chairs are extra?
items.answer: 228 ÷ 7 = 32, remainder 4. So, 32 chairs are needed in each row and 4 chairs are extra.

items.question: Mrs. Kapoor paid for a ring in 4 equal instalments. How much money did she pay each time if the total cost of the ring is ₹6124?
items.answer: 6124 ÷ 4 = 1531. So, Mrs. Kapoor paid ₹1531 each time as an instalment.

items.question: A box can hold 7 cans. There are 8539 cans to be packed. How many boxes are needed to pack the cans? How many cans will be left over?
items.answer: 8539 ÷ 7 = 1219, remainder 6. So, 1219 boxes are needed and 6 cans will be left over.
